package_info.package_name: Unknown (multiple spam/malware packages, not individually named in report)
package_info.package_versions: Multiple (over 1.4 million versions, specific versions not listed)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are part of coordinated campaigns to deliver spam, SEO poisoning, referral scams, and malware. They abuse the npm ecosystem to lure users to malicious or scam websites, and in some cases, deliver malware payloads that steal credentials, mine cryptocurrency, or perform other harmful actions.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: README.md contains a unique, short link to an external website, e.g., https://short.link/abc123
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the package page is viewed, the README displays a short link that entices users to click, redirecting them to a phishing, scam, or malware-hosting website.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages do not typically use README files to direct users to unrelated or suspicious external sites, especially via short links.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal README files provide documentation, not external links to unrelated or malicious content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may link to project homepages or documentation, but not to warez, phishing, or scam sites.
key_indicators: README contains only a short link
Link points to non-project, suspicious, or warez-related sites

required_permissions: filesystem (if user downloads and executes payload)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Website offers download of a password-encrypted zip file containing a ~600MB zero-padded .exe malware payload.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user clicks the link, they are redirected to a threat actor-controlled website that offers a password-protected zip file. Upon extraction and execution, the .exe file runs malware on the victim's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages do not direct users to download and execute large, password-protected binaries from unrelated websites.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package documentation does not facilitate malware delivery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may use password-protected archives for distribution, but not via random npm packages and warez lures.
key_indicators: Download offered via suspicious, non-official website

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware uses DLL side-loading, disables security tools/firewalls, drops additional tools (Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig), steals credentials, and mines cryptocurrency.
malicious_snippets.code_language: Windows executable (compiled binary, not source code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware evades detection, disables security tools, installs additional malware for credential theft and crypto mining, and exfiltrates stolen data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload performs multiple malicious actions typical of advanced malware, including evasion, credential theft, and unauthorized resource use.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should ever deliver or execute such a payload.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; these are all hallmarks of malware.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: README.md contains links with referral IDs to eCommerce sites (e.g., AliExpress).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the package page is viewed and the user clicks the link, they are redirected to an eCommerce site with a referral ID, generating rewards for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README files are being abused to generate referral rewards for attackers, not to provide documentation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package documentation does not contain referral spam.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some open-source projects may use referral links for funding, but not in spam campaigns across thousands of packages.
key_indicators: Mass creation of packages with only referral spam

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: README.md contains links inviting users to join Telegram crypto scam channels.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the package page is viewed and the user clicks the link, they are invited to join a Telegram channel specializing in crypto scams.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README files are being used to lure users into crypto scams.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package documentation does not promote scam channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate projects may link to community channels, but not to scam or spam groups.
key_indicators: Links to Telegram channels in README

attack_chain.action: Malicious/spam package is published to npm with a README containing a short link or referral/scam link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is enticed to click the link.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the link in the README, which redirects to a phishing, malware, or scam website.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is exposed to malware download, referral scam, or crypto scam.

attack_chain.action: If the user downloads and executes the malware payload, their system is infected.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware executes, stealing credentials, mining crypto, and further compromising the system.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with README files containing only short links or referral links
Packages with no functional code, only documentation spam
Links in README pointing to warez, phishing, or unrelated eCommerce sites
Distribution of password-protected zip files containing large executables
file_indicators: README.md with only a short link or referral link
No package code or only placeholder files
Presence of links to Telegram channels or warez sites
network_indicators: Shortened URLs (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.) in package documentation
Referral URLs to eCommerce sites (e.g., AliExpress with referral ID)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated systems should flag npm packages whose README files contain only a short link, referral link, or links to suspicious domains, especially if the package contains no functional code. Monitor for packages that direct users to download password-protected archives or executables from non-official sources. Correlate mass publication of similar packages from the same user accounts. Alert on packages with documentation linking to warez, phishing, or scam sites, and on those with links to Telegram channels associated with crypto scams.
